Silicone 3D Printing for Prosthetics & Orthotics | Spectroplast
Industry · Prosthetics
Silicone Prosthetics & Orthotics.

Every patient's situation is unique — and their prosthetics and orthotics should be too. Spectroplast's Silicone Additive Manufacturing enables a fully digital, end-to-end workflow for custom prostheses, orthoses, and epitheses in true silicone.
Spectroplast Redefining Prosthetics & Orthotics Manufacturing

True customisation — from digital scan to finished silicone part — enabling prosthetics and orthotics professionals to deliver better patient outcomes faster and more cost-effectively than ever before.

Traditional orthosis fabrication relies on manual casting, hand-finishing, and multiple fitting iterations. Spectroplast replaces this with a fully digital workflow — from patient scan to finished custom orthopedic appliance in a single step. The result is a precise, comfortable fit that meets each patient's specific anatomical needs, produced faster and at lower cost than conventional methods.
Prostheses — Custom-Made.

Prostheses have long been available only as standardised, ready-made products in a limited range of sizes and forms. For the first time, Silicone Additive Manufacturing makes truly custom-made prostheses accessible — parts that feel and look handcrafted but are produced digitally, at scale, and at a price that reflects modern manufacturing efficiency.
Epitheses — Digital Fabrication of Facial & Body Prosthetics

Silicone Additive Manufacturing enables the digital fabrication of epitheses — including toes, fingers, ears, and noses — with a level of anatomical accuracy, surface quality, and skin-tone matching that manual methods struggle to achieve consistently. Each epithesis is produced directly from a patient scan, eliminating the guesswork and manual skill dependency of traditional fabrication.
3D-Printed Silicone Nets for Neural Recording

How can delicate neural samples remain stable without compromising their integrity? Discover how Spectroplast's 3D-printed TrueSil A35 silicone net helps 3Brain securely position living tissue in CorePlate™ neural recording systems, combining biocompatibility, precise geometry, and consistent performance.

Silicone 3D Printing for Robotics & Soft Automation | Spectroplast

Soft robotics and advanced automation demand components that rigid materials simply cannot deliver. Spectroplast produces end-of-arm tooling, grippers, soft actuators, and compliant interfaces in true silicone — with tunable Shore hardness from A20 to A60, complex geometries, and production-grade surface quality.

Silicone's mechanical flexibility can be precisely tuned across a wide Shore hardness range — from ultra-soft A20 for delicate gripping to firmer A60 for structural actuation. This enables application-specific compliance that TPU or TPE alternatives cannot replicate, in true silicone performance.

Silicone Additive Manufacturing removes the geometric limitations of moulding — enabling internal channels, lattice structures, and fine feature details that are essential for soft actuators and precision grippers. Rapid design iteration means you move from file to functional part in days, accelerating your development cycle.

True silicone is chemically stable, tear-resistant, and inherently safe for contact with humans and sensitive surfaces — making it the material of choice for collaborative robotics and precision handling. Spectroplast silicone components deliver the durability and reliability required for demanding industrial and research environments.

Spectroplast's Silicone Additive Manufacturing enables the production of fully individualised ear devices — hearing aids, earmoulds, in-ear monitors, and noise protection — at scale, without the manual labour traditionally required. Spectroplast is an additive manufacturing (AM) service provider developing material chemistry to print high-resolution medical-grade 3D-printed silicone parts. Currently, Spectroplast is the world’s only AM service manufacturer printing silicone-based parts.
